ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB \parallel CD$, $\angle 1 = 30^\circ$, $\angle 2 = 40^\circ$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle 3$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\because$ AB$\parallel$CD, $\angle 1=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle A=\angle 1=30^\circ$,\\
Also, $\because$ $\angle 2=40^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle 3=\angle A+\angle 2=70^\circ$,\\
Therefore, $\angle 3=\boxed{70^\circ}$

The oblique line AD connects from A to D, the oblique line CB connects from C to B, and the two oblique lines intersect at point E. ∠1 is marked near point D, and is the angle formed by CD and AD; ∠2 is marked near point B, and is the angle formed by AB and CB; ∠3 is marked on the left side of intersection point E, and is the exterior angle at point E of triangle ABE. Then reason: Because AB ∥ CD, and AD is a transversal, the angle at point A in triangle ABE is equal to ∠1, that is, ∠A = 30°. Also because the angle at point B is exactly ∠2, ∠B = 40°. For triangle ABE, ∠3 is the exterior angle at point E, equal to the sum of the two non-adjacent interior angles, therefore ∠3 = ∠A + ∠B = 30° + 40° = 70°.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as two parallel horizontal segments AB at the bottom and CD at the top, with diagonals AD and CB intersecting at E; angle 3 is the exterior angle at E of triangle ABE, using CE as the extension of BE. From the text, use AB ∥ CD, ∠1 = 30°, and ∠2 = 40°. Since AD is a transversal of the parallel lines, the angle at A of triangle ABE equals ∠1, so ∠A = 30°. The angle at B of triangle ABE is ∠2 = 40°. By the exterior angle theorem for triangle ABE, ∠3 = ∠A + ∠B = 30° + 40° = 70°.
